newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia three-month KLIBOR fixed at 8.38 pct.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia three-month KLIBOR fixed at 8.38 pct.

text.p: Malaysia's benchmark three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) was fixed at 8.38 percent at 0300 GMT.
It was at 7.92 percent on Wednesday.
The one-month KLIBOR was fixed at 9.0 percent against 8.0 percent on Wednesday.
KLIBOR is fixed by taking an average of rates offered by various banks in the country.
Money market dealers said the rise in interbank rates was expected after Bank Negara warned of tough steps, including increasing interest rates, to stamp out speculation in the ringgit.
The rise was also triggered by a tightening in liquidity as a result of the central bank's massive intervention in the foreign exchange market on Tuesday, they said.
Dealers said although the actual size of the intervention was not known, it could mop up anything from 2.5 billion to 5.0 billion ringgit from the system.
Settlement of Tuesday's intervention will be on Thursday.
